FINDING_ID: IM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor._verify_remediation_outcomes()` verifies a remediation against the latest global metric value only, not against whether the diagnosed pathology has actually cleared. Location: `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`, in the `improved = ...` logic and success branch. Evidence: for `target == "finding_count"` success is defined as `current_val > old_val`, but the pathology `findings_decline` is emitted only when there is a 3-round monotonic decline with a material drop. A one-round uptick from 2→3 would be marked “SUCCESSFUL” even if the recent three-round window remains declining enough to keep re-triggering the same pathology. Similarly for `kappa_stuck`, any increase above the old value counts as success even if kappa is still <0.01 and the stuck condition remains true. This is a logic error in the verification contract: step success is being inferred from scalar drift, not from resolution of the pathology predicate that justified the remediation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace scalar-only success checks with predicate-aware checks keyed by `pathology_key`. For example: verify `kappa_stuck` by requiring the current effective stuck window not to satisfy `all(k < 0.01)` with findings present; verify `findings_decline` by requiring the last 3 finding counts to no longer meet the decline predicate and recovery threshold; verify `mu_distortion` by requiring `not (mu_increasing and findings_not_increasing)`; keep scalar fallback only for pathologies with no explicit predicate.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` and `record_model_round()` emit the same pathology repeatedly while it remains active, with severity escalation, but they do not suppress re-emission when remediation is already in progress for that pathology. Location: all pathology-emission branches in `record_round()` and `record_model_round()`. Evidence: checks append a fresh `DetectorDiagnosis` every qualifying round based only on `_pathology_counts`; there is no guard of the form `if pathology_key not in self._remediation_state` or equivalent. Prior findings covered repeated emission generally and various state-key mismatches, but the missed defect here is specifically that active remediation does not damp further diagnosis generation. That creates an internal feedback loop: a pathology can keep generating new diagnoses before the prior step’s verification window completes, encouraging duplicate or premature re-application at the integration layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Gate diagnosis emission per pathology while a remediation is pending verification. Example rule: if `pathology_key` is present in `_remediation_state` and `current_round - applied_round < verification_window`, suppress new diagnoses for that pathology and optionally emit only a low-severity “still under verification” status once.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` checks remediation outcomes before self-diagnosis, so a self-adjustment made in `self_diagnose()` is never entered into `_remediation_state` and therefore is never outcome-verified by the same machinery the comments claim applies to “all self-adjustments are logged and P-passed”. Location: end of `record_round()`, where `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` runs before `self_diagnose()`, and inside `self_diagnose()` where parameter changes are applied directly without any call to `set_remediation_state()`. Evidence: self-adjustments mutate `_stuck_window`, `_mu_increase_window`, and `_sensitivity_decay`, but there is no corresponding verification state or later verification path for those adjustments. The docstring asserts expected verification after a window; the implementation does not do it.  
PROPOSED_FIX: When `self_diagnose()` applies a self-adjustment, call `set_remediation_state()` with a dedicated pathology key such as `self_low_remediation_success_rate` or `self_high_false_positive_rate`, target metric matching the trigger (`remediation_success_rate` / `false_positive_rate`), and verify those via an extended metric-history mechanism. Alternatively, move self-adjustment verification into a dedicated self-verification queue if overloading `_remediation_state` is undesirable.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `_get_metric_history()` and remediation verification support only `kappa`, `mu`, `novelty`, `finding_count`, and `vocab_growth`, but the self-diagnosis subsystem reasons over `remediation_success_rate`, `false_positive_rate`, and `chain_exhaustion_rate`. Location: `_get_metric_history()` and `_verify_remediation_outcomes()`. Evidence: there is no way to express those self-layer metrics as `target_metric` values for verification, which confirms the self-adjustment verification path is structurally incomplete, not just omitted in one caller. This is an interface mismatch inside the immune layer.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Extend metric access/verification support to include immune meta-metrics, e.g. `remediation_success_rate`, `false_positive_rate`, and `chain_exhaustion_rate`, each computed over explicit round-stamped histories. Then use those metric names when recording self-adjustment state.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `check_dispatch_health()` bypasses the same diagnosis-registration discipline used elsewhere and directly appends to `self._diagnoses`, but unlike `record_round()` it does so before any remediation outcome verification or self-diagnosis consolidation. Location: final lines of `check_dispatch_health()`. Evidence: `record_model_round()` was explicitly changed to avoid direct mutation, and `register_diagnoses()` exists to centralize external diagnosis registration, but `check_dispatch_health()` still performs `self._diagnoses.extend(new_diagnoses)` itself. A prior finding noted the bypass generally; the missed consequence is that dispatch-health diagnoses contaminate `false_positive_rate` and other retrospective meta-metrics at a different point in the control cycle than detector diagnoses, so metric windows depend on call ordering outside the class.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove direct append from `check_dispatch_health()` and require the caller to pass returned diagnoses through `register_diagnoses()` in a consistent phase, or have `record_round()` accept and consolidate dispatch-health diagnoses in one place.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` uses `effective_window("kappa", self._stuck_window)` and `effective_window("mu", self._mu_increase_window)`, where `effective_window` depends on `_pathology_counts[detector]`. But `_pathology_counts` for those detectors is incremented every time the pathology re-fires and is only reset on certain resolution paths; while remediation is active and pathology persists, the window shrinks further each round, making rediagnosis increasingly easier. Location: nested `effective_window()` plus the kappa/mu branches. Evidence: `persistent = self._pathology_counts.get(detector, 0)` feeds `narrow = 1 / (1 + growth * persistent)`. For a still-active pathology, repeated diagnoses increase persistence, which reduces the threshold window and increases detection frequency, even though no new independent evidence has arrived. This is effectively integral wind-up tied to diagnosis count, not pathology episodes.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base adaptive sensitivity on episode count or verified persistence duration rather than raw repeated diagnosis count. At minimum, stop incrementing `_pathology_counts` once the pathology is active until it resolves, or separate `active_episode` from `repeat_emissions`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` does not emit any event for `UNDERPERFORM`, even though all higher-priority failure types emit `ManagerEvent`s and the class docstring advertises a real-time monitoring interface. Location: `detect_failure()`, under the priority-5 branch. Evidence: on underperformance the method returns `FailureType.UNDERPERFORM` directly with no `_emit_event(...)` call. That makes the event stream incomplete and asymmetric across failure types, which breaks observability and any external monitor relying on the event callback contract.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit a `ManagerEvent` for underperformance before returning, with event type `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` if available, otherwise add it to the enum and use a detailed payload including `perf`, `theta_under`, window size, and recent performance history summary.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `FailureHandler._performance_metric()` depends on `response.finding_count` and `response.mean_abstraction`, but the shown `ModelResponse` declaration is skeletal and therefore the method’s required input contract is not visible or enforceable within the excerpt. This is not just “code missing”; it is an immune-boundary interface risk because failure detection correctness depends on those fields being present and populated before `detect_failure()`. Evidence: `_performance_metric()` directly reads both fields; the displayed `ModelResponse` class stub provides no assurance, and the interface summary only names `ModelResponse` generically. Given CDSFL fail-closed requirements, this unassessed dependency should not be treated as safe.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make the dependency explicit in the immune boundary by either: (a) validating in `detect_failure()` that `ModelResponse` has `finding_count` and `mean_abstraction` and fail closed with a typed event if absent, or (b) moving underperformance inputs into explicit parameters passed from `process_round()` rather than assuming hidden fields.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: IM_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.60  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: `self_diagnose()` can emit multiple self-diagnosis findings in one call after applying a self-adjustment in self-check 2, because unlike the earlier low-success-rate branch there is no early return or suppression before self-check 3. Location: `self_diagnose()`, after the high false-positive-rate adjustment branch. Evidence: when self-check 2 adjusts `_sensitivity_decay` and sets `_last_self_adjust_round`, execution continues immediately into the chain-exhaustion branch in the same call. Earlier rounds already had similar bugs for checks 1 and 3 combinations; this remaining 2→3 path is still open.  
PROPOSED_FIX: After any self-adjustment is applied in self-diagnose, return immediately for that round, or centralize self-check scheduling so at most one self-diagnosis action can be emitted per call.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The review boundary explicitly includes `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis()`, `_apply_transform()`, and `process_round()` immune integration, but those implementations are not present in the artifact, so several high-risk claims cannot be verified honestly: whether pending-remediation suppression is respected, whether chain lengths are passed consistently after all fixes, whether transforms are idempotent, and whether every mutating immune action has explicit timeout/ordering semantics in the call chain. Evidence: the excerpt contains only interface summaries or references for those components. Under CDSFL fail-closed rules, this means any claim that no additional issues exist in those omitted areas would be unsupported.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Provide the actual definitions of `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis()`, `_apply_transform()`, and the relevant `process_round()` body for verification. Without them, immune-layer review coverage is incomplete by construction.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

Definitive stance: I found 10 missed issues, with 7 verified directly from the shown code and 3 explicitly marked unverified because the necessary integration code or full type definitions were omitted.
